conventions.convention: An admissible patch has dimension two or three, is globally injective and bi-Lipschitz on the closed reference cube, has positive cell Jacobians, and has a bounded Lipschitz physical image with the specified finite cell-boundary presentation. Positive weights alone provide none of these geometric certificates.

The analysis space is S_h/W using the fixed geometry denominator and an analysis grid refining the geometry grid. Conforming trial spaces additionally impose global H1 or H1_0 membership; multipatch field traces must agree componentwise.

Scalar gradients are columns; vector fields use row gradients, giving physical vector gradient (reference gradient) DF inverse. The unit-Laplace pullback tensor is det(DF) DF inverse DF inverse-transpose.
The global lower Lipschitz constant c is separate from the local inverse-derivative bound L. Perturbed-map admissibility also retains a boundary certificate or the stated C1 extension alternative.

The Greville comparison permits interior multiplicity p+1, uses the specified canonical knot-value convention, and preserves continuity through equal sampled endpoint coefficients. Its constants retain degree dependence; the comparison operator need not be a projector.

The multipatch approximation branch requires aligned tangential grids and degrees under permutations/reflections, proportional positive face denominators, and corresponding proportional smooth numerator traces.

The Sobolev, conformity and energy branches assume Countable Choice. The tensorized conditional L2 quasi-interpolation theorem instead explicitly assumes the Axiom of Choice and supplied bounded coordinate extensions, commutation, section regularity and measurability.
Geometry, quadrature and load defects remain separate; discrete coercivity is assumed. All defects are zero by definition for the zero trial space.

load_bearing.statement: Under Countable Choice and the stated admissible-map bounds, pullback and inverse pullback preserve H1, satisfy the displayed norm bounds, and map H1_0 onto H1_0; the cellwise weak chain rule and scalar/vector energy transformations hold.

Under Countable Choice, a field C1 on each closed cell of the specified finite face-to-face partition, with square-integrable cell gradients and equal one-sided values on shared faces, belongs to global H1 with its piecewise classical gradient.
The finite positive-weight tensor basis satisfies w_- ≤ W ≤ w_+, R_alpha ≥ 0, sum R_alpha = 1, and N_h = S_h/W, with the stated cellwise quotient derivative and derivative bound.

Under its Countable Choice, admissible-map, positive continuous denominator and matching cellwise C1 hypotheses, v_h = (s/W) composed with F inverse belongs to H1 and the physical H1 error is at most C_F C_W times the numerator H1 error.

For the stated finite clamped grids with degrees at least one and C1,1 data, the explicit tensor Greville sampled spline is continuous, satisfies the displayed value and cell-gradient bounds, and under Countable Choice has H1 error at most M_g B. It preserves zero faces and the specified aligned face identifications.

For the stated admissible maps with derivative and inverse bounds at most M, the unit-Laplace tensor difference is at most (d M^(d+1) + 2 M^(d+3)) times the essential-supremum derivative-map error, with the corresponding gradient-pairing bound.
Assume Countable Choice. Let U be open and let z belong to H1(U) and vanish almost everywhere outside a compact subset of U. Then z belongs to H1_0(U).

concerns.concern: The Statement says D=(0,2)×(0,1) is 'the union' of D_L=(0,1)×(0,1) and D_R=(1,2)×(0,1). Their union omits {1}×(0,1). The intended partition is up to the shared face, and v needs an arbitrary value there to be a literal function on D. This is a presentation issue: the missing face is null and the weak-derivative contradiction in the proof is valid on the stated full rectangle.

seams_checked.note: Opened the insertion algorithm and curve-preservation theorem. The homogeneous consumer uses only a new knot strictly inside a positive span, applies the same zero-based control update to homogeneous slices, and divides by the unchanged positive denominator. It does not infer general degree elevation or existing-knot insertion from this supplier.

Opened both curved-geometry definitions. The adapter supplies matching parameter-coordinate simplices, smooth neighborhood extensions and neighborhood injectivity, positive determinants and finite derivative bounds. It preserves the geometry errors and distinguishes within-mesh trace matching from equality of the two exterior boundaries. Rational analysis functions are not treated as affine P1 functions.

Opened the displacement definition and Galerkin theorem. The consumer retains the real full-Dirichlet space, dimensions two or three, bounded connected Lipschitz domain, measurable positive shear bounds, finite nonnegative lambda, bounded load, Countable Choice and the exact factor (2 mu_1+d lambda)/mu_0. It makes no locking-free inference.
